family.description: Members of this family are integral membrane proteins. This family includes a protein with hemolytic activity from Bacillus cereus [[cite:PUB00019707]]. It has been proposed that YOL002c encodes a Saccharomyces cerevisiae protein that plays a key role in metabolic pathways that regulate lipid and phosphate metabolism [[cite:PUB00019708]]. In eukaryotes, members are seven-transmembrane pass molecules found to encode functional receptors with a broad range of apparent ligand specificities, including progestin and adipoQ receptors, and hence have been named PAQR proteins [[cite:PUB00071573]]. The mammalian members include progesterone binding proteins [[cite:PUB00071574]]. Unlike the case with GPCR receptor proteins, the evolutionary ancestry of the members of this family can be traced back to the Archaea. This family belongs to the CREST superfamily [[cite:PUB00085069]], which are distantly related to GPCRs.
family.name: Haemolysin-III related
